question.:question/problem:
$$
f(t,y)=⟨\text{_____},\,y,\,8\sec  t⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,y)$ above parametrizes one sheet of the hyperbolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${z}^{2}-{x}^{2}=64$ for $z\ge 8.$ What is the first component of $f?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the hyperbola ${z}^{2}-{x}^{2}=64$ for $z\ge 8$ in $xz$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,\,z⟩=⟨8\tan  t,\,8\sec  t⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

since 

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{2}-{x}^{2} & =(8\sec  t)^{2}-(8\tan  t)^{2} \\  & =64(\sec^{2} t-\tan^{2} t) \\  & =64.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t,y) & =⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩ \\  & =⟨8\tan  t,\,y,\,8\sec  t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})$ and $y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $8\tan  t.$

question.:question/problem:
$$
f(t,x)=⟨x,\,9\sec  t,\,\text{_____}⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,x)$ above parametrizes one sheet of the hyperbolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $7{y}^{2}-81{z}^{2}=567$ for $y\ge 9.$ What is the third component of $f?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the hyperbola

$$
7{y}^{2}-81{z}^{2}=567\,⇒\,\frac{{y}^{2}}{{9}^{2}}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{(\sqrt{7})^{2}}=1
$$

for $y\ge 9$ in $yz$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨y,\,z⟩=⟨9\sec  t,\,\sqrt{7}\tan  t⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

since 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}}{{9}^{2}}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{(\sqrt{7})^{2}} & =\frac{(9\sec  t)^{2}}{81}-\frac{(\sqrt{7}\tan  t)^{2}}{7} \\  & =\frac{81\sec^{2} t}{81}-\frac{7\tan^{2} t}{7} \\  & =\sec^{2} t-\tan^{2} t \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t,x) & =⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩ \\  & =⟨x,\,9\sec  t,\,\sqrt{7}\tan  t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})$ and $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $\sqrt{7}\tan  t.$

The vector-valued function $f(y, t)$ above parametrizes one sheet of the hyperbolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $7x^{2} - 81z^{2} = 567$ for $x \ge 9$. What is the third component of $f$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the hyperbola $\frac{x^2}{81}-\frac{z^2}{7}=1$ for $x\ge 9$ in $xz$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,\,z⟩=⟨9\sec t,\,\sqrt{7}\tan t⟩,\quad t\in(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2})
$$

since 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x^2}{81}-\frac{z^2}{7}&=\frac{(9\sec t)^2}{81}-\frac{(\sqrt{7}\tan t)^2}{7}\\&=\frac{81\sec^2 t}{81}-\frac{7\tan^2 t}{7}\\&=\sec^2 t-\tan^2 t\\&=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y,t)&=⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩\\&=⟨9\sec t,\,y,\,\sqrt{7}\tan t⟩\end{aligned}

where $t\in(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2})$ and $y\in(-\infty,\infty).$

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $\sqrt{7}\tan t.$

question.:question/problem:
$f(x, t) = ⟨x, _____, 6\sec t⟩, t ∈ (-\frac{π}{2}, \frac{π}{2})$

The vector-valued function $f(x, t)$ above parametrizes one sheet of the hyperbolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $2z^{2} - 36y^{2} = 72$ for $z \ge 6$. What is the second component of $f$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the hyperbola $\frac{z^2}{36}-\frac{y^2}{2}=1$ for $z\ge 6$ in $yz$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨y,z⟩=⟨\sqrt{2}\tan t,\,6\sec t⟩,\quad t\in(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2})
$$

since 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{z^2}{36}-\frac{y^2}{2}&=\frac{(6\sec t)^2}{36}-\frac{(\sqrt{2}\tan t)^2}{2}\\&=\frac{36\sec^2 t}{36}-\frac{2\tan^2 t}{2}\\&=\sec^2 t-\tan^2 t\\&=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,t)&=⟨x,y,z⟩\\&=⟨x,\,\sqrt{2}\tan t,\,6\sec t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2})$ and $x\in(-\infty,\infty).$

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $\sqrt{2}\tan t.$
